item.title: John Dickinson: Forgotten Founder | Fall 2025, Vol 70, No 4
item.description: Dickinson played a pivotal role in our Nation’s founding, from the Stamp Act to ratifying the Constitution, but his contributions are largely forgotten by history. John Dickinson (right) stands off to the side among the statues of Signers at the National Constitution Center. George Washington stands at the left before a table at which Benjamin Franklin sits. Photo by Edwin Grosvenor

item.title: Still “Crazy” for Patsy Cline | Fall 2025, Vol 70, No 4
item.description: Since her untimely death in 1963, the legendary country music star—and the first female to be inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame—continues to inspire new audiences and artists. Despite her career lasting only a handful of years, Cline has gone down as one of the most influential female vocalists in country music history. item.title: The Birth of Birthright Citizenship | Fall 2025, Vol 70, No 4
item.description: A Chinatown cook's fight to re-enter the U.S. in 1895 went up to the Supreme Court, which upheld his claim to birthright citizenship and guaranteed it for all through the 14th Amendment. Although Wong Kim Ark was born and grew up in the U.S., he was denied re-entry in 1895 after a trip to visit family in China. National Archives
